newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilians back Cardoro running for new term - poll.
newsitem.headline: Brazilians back Cardoro running for new term - poll.

text.p: A slim majority of Brazilians believe the constitution should be rewritten to give President Fernando Henrique Cardoso a chance to run for re-election, according to a poll released on Friday.
But a third of the Brazilian voters polled did not fully understand what re-election means.

The poll, published in newspapers O Globo and O Estado de Sao Paulo, said 51 percent of respondents favoured rewriting the constitution to allow Cardoso to run again in 1998. Another 19 percent favoured re-election only for future presidents, while 25 percent opposed re-election.

The findings contrasted with those of a September poll which put opposition to Cardoso's re-election at 62 percent. But the latest survey also showed 19 percent did not know what the term re-election meant.
Fourteen percent of the voters believed re-election meant office holders would have their terms renewed automatically at the end of their mandate, according to the survey.

Brazil's constitution limits presidents, as well as state governors and mayors, to one term. Congress this month is due to begin discussing a proposed constitutional amendment that would allow Cardoso, as well as governors and mayors, to run for a second term.
The poll was taken by the private Brazilian Public Opinion Institute, which surveyed 2,000 voters between Sept. 20-23. No margin of error was given.
